safety_warnings: ALWAYS unplug the fan from power outlet before any repair work
Wait at least 5 minutes after unplugging before touching internal components
Do NOT touch the capacitor terminals directly - it may hold residual charge
Do NOT operate the fan without the front guard installed
Do NOT use the fan if power cord is damaged or frayed
Keep water away from motor and electrical components
Do NOT bypass the thermal fuse permanently - it is a safety device
diagnostic_steps: Step 1: Check power cord - plug into working outlet and test with multimeter for continuity
Step 2: Check thermal fuse - use multimeter continuity mode on fuse terminals inside motor housing
Step 3: Check capacitor - look for bulging, leaking, or burnt marks on the capacitor
Step 4: Check speed switch - test each speed position with multimeter for continuity
Step 5: Check motor winding - test resistance between speed wires (blue=common, yellow=speed2, red=speed3)
Step 6: Check bushing - spin the blade by hand, if it feels rough or stuck, bushing needs replacement
Step 7: Check oscillation gearbox - remove gearbox cover and inspect gears for wear or broken teeth
repair_steps: Step 1: Unplug fan and remove front guard by turning guard fixing ring counterclockwise
Step 2: Remove blade nut (WARNING: reverse thread - turn CLOCKWISE to loosen)
Step 3: Pull off fan blade from motor shaft
Step 4: Remove rear guard by unscrewing guard fixing ring
Step 5: Open switch box cover by removing screws at bottom
Step 6: Photograph all wire connections before disconnecting anything
Step 7: For thermal fuse replacement - remove motor housing screws, carefully extract windings
Step 8: Locate thermal fuse embedded in windings - it looks like a small cylinder with two wires
Step 9: Cut old thermal fuse wires, solder new thermal fuse (same rating) in place
Step 10: Cover with heat shrink tube, carefully reassemble windings into motor housing
Step 11: For capacitor replacement - note the microfarad rating on old capacitor, replace with same rating
Step 12: For bushing replacement - remove motor shaft, pull out old bushing, press in new one with light oil
Step 13: Reassemble in reverse order, test on each speed before putting back the guard
common_failures: Thermal fuse blown - most common cause of completely dead fan, fuse embedded in motor winding
Capacitor failed - causes slow rotation, humming without spinning, or fan only works on highest speed
Bushing worn out - causes grinding noise, heavy/slow rotation, motor shaft wobbles
Speed switch contacts corroded - fan works on some speeds but not others
Power cord internal break - fan intermittently dies when cord is moved
Oscillation gear teeth broken - oscillation stops but fan still spins normally

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan completely dead, no response at all
troubleshooting_table.cause: Thermal fuse blown or power cord break
troubleshooting_table.solution: Test power cord continuity first. If OK, open motor housing and test thermal fuse. Replace if open circuit.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Motor hums but blade won't spin
troubleshooting_table.solution: Try spinning blade by hand while powered on. If it starts, replace capacitor. If shaft is stiff, replace bushing.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan spins slowly on all speeds
troubleshooting_table.solution: Check bushing for roughness. Replace capacitor with same uF rating if bushing is OK.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Capacitor partially failed or switch contact issue
troubleshooting_table.solution: Replace capacitor. If still fails, check speed switch wire connections with multimeter.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Stator winding shorted or thermal fuse about to blow
troubleshooting_table.solution: STOP using immediately. Unplug. Check winding resistance. If reading is very low or zero, winding is shorted - replace motor.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Oscillation not working but fan spins fine
troubleshooting_table.cause: Oscillation gear teeth broken or knob mechanism stuck
troubleshooting_table.solution: Open gearbox cover. Inspect gears for broken teeth. Clean and lubricate. Replace gear if broken.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan vibrates and makes rattling noise
troubleshooting_table.cause: Loose blade nut, unbalanced blade, or loose guard
troubleshooting_table.solution: Tighten blade nut (reverse thread!). Check blade for cracks. Ensure all guards are secure.

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean fan blades and guards with damp cloth
Clean switch box area from dust, check power cord condition
Apply 2-3 drops of light machine oil to front and rear bushing
Open motor housing, clean dust from winding, inspect capacitor and thermal fuse

safety_warnings: ALWAYS unplug the fan before any repair - wall outlet may be hard to reach, use circuit breaker if needed
Wall fan is mounted at height - use stable ladder, never stand on chair
Support the fan body before removing wall mount screws - fan can fall and cause injury
Capacitor may hold charge even after unplugging - discharge with insulated screwdriver
Check wall mount bracket for cracks before remounting repaired fan
Do NOT operate without front guard - blade at eye level is extremely dangerous
diagnostic_steps: Step 1: Ensure power outlet works - test with another device
Step 2: Check power cord for damage or internal break - test with multimeter
Step 3: Remove fan from wall mount carefully using ladder
Step 4: Open motor housing - check thermal fuse with multimeter continuity test
Step 5: Inspect capacitor for bulging, leaking, or burn marks
Step 6: Check speed selector switch - test each position with multimeter
Step 7: Test motor winding resistance between each speed wire and common wire
Step 8: Check pull cord mechanism if applicable - inspect for broken cord or stuck switch
repair_steps: Step 1: Unplug fan. Use ladder to safely remove fan from wall bracket
Step 2: Place fan on flat surface. Remove front guard (turn fixing ring counterclockwise)
Step 3: Remove blade nut (usually reverse thread - turn CLOCKWISE to loosen)
Step 4: Remove fan blade and rear guard
Step 5: Open motor housing by removing housing screws
Step 6: For thermal fuse: locate in winding, cut old fuse, solder new one (same temp rating)
Step 7: For capacitor: disconnect old capacitor wires, connect new one with same uF and voltage rating
Step 8: For pull cord: remove switch housing, replace pull cord mechanism
Step 9: Reassemble motor housing, ensure no wires are pinched
Step 10: Reassemble blade, guards, and test on each speed
Step 11: Remount on wall - check bracket is secure, use appropriate wall anchors
common_failures: Thermal fuse blown - fan completely dead, most common failure
Capacitor degraded - fan hums or spins slowly, especially on low speed
Pull cord switch broken - cord pulls out but doesn't click or change speed
Wall mount bracket loosened - fan tilts or falls from wall, dangerous
Bushing dry or worn - grinding noise, slow start, motor gets hot quickly
Speed selector contacts worn - fan works on some speeds only

troubleshooting_table.cause: Thermal fuse blown or power cord issue
troubleshooting_table.solution: Check power cord first. Then open motor and test thermal fuse for continuity. Replace if blown.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan hums but blade doesn't move
troubleshooting_table.solution: Give blade a manual push. If it starts spinning, replace capacitor. If shaft is stuck, replace bushing and add oil.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Pull cord switch mechanism broken internally
troubleshooting_table.solution: Replace entire pull cord switch unit. Match wire colors when reconnecting.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Loose wall bracket screws or wall anchors pulled out
troubleshooting_table.solution: Remove fan. Install new wall anchors if needed. Retighten bracket. Ensure bracket is level.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan gets very hot after 30 minutes
troubleshooting_table.cause: Bushing dry, winding partially shorted, or blocked ventilation
troubleshooting_table.solution: Clean dust from motor vents. Oil bushings. If still hot, check winding resistance - may need motor replacement.

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean blades and guards from dust with damp cloth
Clean motor vents and switch housing from dust
Oil bushings with 2-3 drops of light machine oil through front and rear shaft openings
Full disassembly, clean winding from dust, inspect capacitor and thermal fuse, check wall bracket condition

symptoms: fan stops after running few minutes
safety_warnings: ALWAYS unplug fan before opening or repairing
Do NOT touch capacitor terminals - may hold residual charge
Do NOT run fan without front guard - especially around children
Do NOT use fan if power cord shows any damage
Keep fan away from water and wet surfaces
If burning smell occurs, unplug IMMEDIATELY and do not use until repaired
Do NOT force blade nut - remember it is usually REVERSE THREAD (clockwise to loosen)
diagnostic_steps: Step 1: Verify power outlet is working with another device
Step 2: Check power cord - wiggle cord near plug and near fan entry point while testing with multimeter
Step 3: Open switch box or base cover - check for loose or burnt wire connections
Step 4: Test thermal fuse continuity with multimeter - located inside motor winding
Step 5: Inspect capacitor visually - look for bulging top, leaking fluid, or burn marks
Step 6: Test capacitor with multimeter capacitance mode if available
Step 7: Test rotary switch - check continuity at each speed position
Step 8: Spin blade by hand - if rough or grinding, bushing is worn
Step 9: Smell the motor area - burnt smell indicates possible winding damage
repair_steps: Step 1: Unplug fan completely
Step 2: Remove front guard - either unclip or turn fixing ring counterclockwise
Step 3: Remove blade nut - REVERSE THREAD, turn CLOCKWISE to loosen
Step 4: Pull blade off motor shaft gently
Step 5: Remove rear guard
Step 6: Open motor housing screws (usually 4 screws around the housing)
Step 7: Take photo of all wire connections before disconnecting
Step 8: For thermal fuse: locate small cylinder in winding, cut old wires, solder new fuse with same temperature rating, insulate with heat shrink
Step 9: For capacitor: note uF and voltage rating, desolder old one, solder new one matching specs
Step 10: For rotary switch: unsolder wires from old switch, install new switch, reconnect wires matching photo from step 7
Step 11: For bushing: pull motor shaft out, remove old bushing, insert new bushing, add 2-3 drops oil
Step 12: Reassemble motor housing - make sure no wires pinched between housing halves
Step 13: Reattach rear guard, blade (reverse thread nut!), front guard
Step 14: Test on all speed settings before use
common_failures: Thermal fuse blown - number one cause of dead fan, fuse is inside motor winding and opens when overheated
Capacitor degraded - causes slow spin or motor humming without rotation, very common in fans older than 2 years
Bushing worn - metal sleeve bearing dries out, causes grinding noise and slow heavy rotation
Rotary switch contacts burnt - switch feels loose, fan only works on some speeds or no speed at all
Power cord internal wire break - fan dies intermittently, especially when cord is moved or bent
Oscillation gear cracked - oscillation stops but fan still rotates, plastic gear teeth wear out over time

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan completely dead, no response when plugged in
troubleshooting_table.cause: Blown thermal fuse (90% of cases) or broken power cord
troubleshooting_table.solution: Test power cord with multimeter first. If cord is OK, open motor housing and test thermal fuse continuity. Replace blown fuse with same temperature rating (usually 115-120 degree Celsius).

troubleshooting_table.problem: Motor hums/buzzes but blade doesn't spin
troubleshooting_table.solution: Try pushing blade gently by hand while fan is on. If it starts spinning, capacitor is bad - replace it. If shaft won't turn freely by hand when unplugged, bushing is seized - replace and oil.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan runs but very slowly on all speeds
troubleshooting_table.solution: Replace capacitor with exact same uF rating. Also add oil to front and rear bushings.

troubleshooting_table.problem: Fan works on speed 3 only, not on 1 and 2
troubleshooting_table.solution: Replace capacitor. Lower speeds need more capacitor assistance to start.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Worn bushing, loose blade, or debris in housing
troubleshooting_table.solution: Check blade for wobble. Open housing and inspect bushing. Clean any debris. Replace bushing if worn.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Thermal fuse cutting out due to overheating, then resets
troubleshooting_table.solution: Motor is overheating - likely dry bushing causing friction heat. Oil bushings. If problem persists, winding may be partially shorted.

troubleshooting_table.cause: Winding insulation burning or capacitor failing
troubleshooting_table.solution: STOP immediately. Unplug. Open housing and inspect for burn marks. Test winding resistance. Replace damaged component.

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean blades and guards from dust with damp cloth
Check power cord for any damage or fraying
Clean base and switch area, check rubber feet
Oil front and rear bushings with 2-3 drops light machine oil
Full service - open motor housing, clean dust from winding, inspect capacitor and thermal fuse, replace bushing oil
